title: O, Stay Thy Tears! for They Are Blest
description: O, Stay Thy Tears! for They Are Blest in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Andrews Norton wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 346, “O, Stay Thy Tears!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, stay thy tears! for they are blest Whose days are past, whose toil is done; Here mid-night care dis-turbs our rest, Here sor-row dims the morn-ing sun.

lines: O, stay thy tears! for they are blest
Whose days are past, whose toil is done;
Here midnight care disturbs our rest,
Here sorrow dims the morning sun.
For laboring virtue's anxious toil,
For patient sorrow's stifled sigh,
For faith that marks the conqueror's spoil,
Heaven grants the recompense, — to die.
How blest are they whose transient years
Pass like an evening meteor's flight,
Not dark with guilt, nor dim with tears,
Whose course is short, unclouded, bright!
O, cheerless were our lengthened way,
But heaven's own light dispels the gloom,
Streams downward from eternal day,
And sheds a glory round the tomb!
Then stay thy tears, — the blest above
Have hailed a spirit's heavenly birth,
Sung a new song of joy and love;
Then why should anguish reign on earth?

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Andrews Norton died in 1853.
credits: Words by Andrews Norton (1786–1853), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
